html:
Chogha Zanbil is a great stepped temple, a ziggurat, built around 1250 BCE by Untash-Napirisha, king of Elam, in Khuzestan in southwestern Iran. It is one of the few ziggurats outside Mesopotamia and among the best preserved.

It stood at the heart of a new religious city, Dur Untash, with temples for many gods of Elam and of Mesopotamia. Thousands of its baked bricks bear inscriptions in Elamite. Its walls held a water system that brought water from a river miles away. The city was left unfinished after the king's death and was sacked by Assyria under Ashurbanipal around 640 BCE.

Found by oil prospectors in 1935, it became Iran's first World Heritage Site in 1979. Compare the Ziggurat of Ur.
